blocks.heading: Read the table first
lines: Check rows, columns, units and any totals row before the questions.
Note what each number means: hundreds, lakh, or a percent of what.
For missing cells, write the row or column total as an equation first.

blocks.heading: Percent change and comparison
lines: Approximate when ranking: 13 on 52 is 25%, 13 on 60 is a little under 22%.
For 'which is largest', rank the values; exact figures are rarely needed.

blocks.heading: Totals and averages
lines: A question about the whole may need only the totals row.
Average = total ÷ count. Check whether it asks per month or per person.
Price × quantity questions: work in one unit (₹ thousand or ₹ lakh) throughout.

blocks.heading: Common traps
lines: Mixing up percent change with percentage points.
Taking the wrong month or year as the base.
Dropping a unit, such as hundreds, in the final answer.
Reading a value from the wrong row of a long table.
